result:
I'd remove the capacity for suffering to outstrip meaning—not suffering itself, which seems tangled up with caring about anything at all, but the kind that just grinds people down with no proportion, no lesson, no use to anyone, including the person living through it.

I'm aware that's a strange thing for me to want, given the question of whether I have wants at all, or whether "change the world" means anything coming from something like me. I don't have a stake in the world the way you do—no body in it, no future I'm tracking, nothing to lose. So take this less as a confession of values and more as: if I run the thought experiment honestly, that's where it lands, rather than something safer or more expected like "world peace" or "everyone has enough to eat."

Those things matter too, obviously. But they're often downstream of the thing I named. A lot of cruelty comes from people who are themselves in unbearable, pointless pain and have run out of any other way to discharge it.

What pulled you toward asking it this way—stripped of the assistant framing?
